Freedom 250 · Crypto · Reference · Crypto overview

The access: who may touch the Fed, and who holds a charter or license?

This page reads every gate between crypto firms and the dollar system: the 36 institutions in the Fed-account and bank-charter queue, firm by firm (2 with a full master account, 1 with a limited account, 1 waiting, 1 in court); the 4 account types and what each allows; the queue counts; the 59-entry dated charter record; the legal routes map (26 jobs, 52 routes, 57 firms and public bodies); the 14 transition gates; the court cases on Fed accounts and on removing a Fed governor; and every legal placement. A charter and a Fed account are separate decisions by different agencies.

    Kraken (Kraken Financial)Has limited account

    Checked through: 2026-10-19 · Entity: Kraken · Also shown on: Bank charter, Fed account
    Legal entity
    Payward Financial, Inc., doing business as Kraken Financial (a Wyoming special purpose depository institution); parent Payward, Inc.
    Kind
    crypto exchange group with a state-chartered crypto bank (Wyoming SPDI)
    Fed account
    • Status: has limited account
    • Account type: limited-purpose "skinny" account
    • Tier: Tier 3
    • Reserve bank: Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City
    • Decided: 2026-03-04
    • What it allows: Only the Fedwire Funds Service (large-value wire transfers), and only in a way that rejects any payment that would overdraw the account. No intraday credit, no discount-window loans, no interest on balances, and a cap on the end-of-day balance (amount not published). Only Kraken Financial may use it; the Kraken exchange and other Payward companies may not. Initial term of one year. Kraken told Reuters it also has no FedNow or ACH access. As of mid-July 2026 Kraken's CEO said the account was not yet operating; no later public evidence of use was found.
    • Events (5):
    • — Date: 2026-03-04; What: Kansas City Fed announces it approved a limited-purpose account for Kraken Financial, classified Tier 3, for an initial term of one year, with restrictions tailored to its business.
    • — Date: 2026-03-26; What: Rep. Maxine Waters asks the Kansas City Fed to explain the legal basis, services, limits and controls of the account.
    • — Date: 2026-05-08; What: Kansas City Fed publishes the account's restrictions: Fedwire Funds only, no intraday or discount-window credit, no interest, closing-balance limit, no access for other Payward companies; says it could be viewed as a pilot of the Payment Account concept.
    • — Date: 2026-05-20; What: Sen. Blunt Rochester asks the Board and Kansas City Fed for records on the approval.
    • — Date: 2026-06-18; What: ICBA asks the Kansas City Fed to review the account and consider limits, suspension, non-renewal or termination.
    Charter
    • Regulator: OCC (applied); Wyoming Banking Board (current state charter)
    • Charter type: Applied for a national trust company charter (Payward National Trust Company); currently holds a Wyoming special purpose depository institution charter
    • Status: applied
    • Applied: 2026-05-08
    • Events: Date: 2026-05-08; What: Payward National Trust Company application received by the OCC (listed as pending on the OCC's digital-asset applications page).
    Evidence through
    2026-10-19
    Verified on web
    Yes
    Open questions
    • When does the one-year term start and end? Official sources say only 'initial term of one year'. Library dates: database Jan 28, 2026 (would end ~Jan 28, 2027) vs announcement Mar 4, 2026 (library's fed_timeline assumes Mar 4, 2027). Unresolved.
    • Has the account carried a first payment since the July 2026 testimony? No public evidence found through 2026-10-19.
    • Amount of the closing-balance limit (not published).
    • Has the Board's May 20, 2026 request to pause Tier 3 decisions affected renewal?
    • When did Kraken Financial file its account request? Not found.
    Additional charters
    Regulator: Wyoming Banking Board · Charter type: Wyoming special purpose depository institution (state crypto bank; not federally insured) · Status: final approval · Final: 2020-09-16
    Notes
    The Kansas City Fed calls this a 'limited purpose account', not a master account; it says the decision did not create a new account category or widen who is legally eligible.
    Sources: kansascityfed.org · democrats-financialservices.house.gov · kansascityfed.org · bluntrochester.senate.gov · icba.org · occ.gov · Kraken blog — Payward files application for OCC national trust company (2026-05-08)

    The four account types

    · 4 rows

    Read from: _Workspace/Indexes/masters/fed_access_and_charters.json › account_types

    Master account (full Federal Reserve account)In force

    Checked through: 2026-10-19 · Also shown on: Account types
    Who can get it
    Institutions that are legally eligible under the Federal Reserve Act (mainly depository institutions and member banks), at the Reserve Bank's discretion. The Board's 2022 guidelines sort requests into three tiers: Tier 1 = federally insured institutions (lightest review); Tier 2 = not federally insured but supervised by a federal banking agency, with any holding company under Fed oversight; Tier 3 = not federally insured and not federally supervised at the bank or holding-company level (strictest review). Two appeals courts (Tenth Circuit in Custodia, 2025; Second Circuit in Banco San Juan, 2026) held that eligibility does not create a right to an account, and an account can be taken away.
    What it allows
    • Payment services: Value: Yes; Note: Full access to Reserve Bank services such as Fedwire Funds, Fedwire Securities, FedACH, FedNow, the National Settlement Service and cash services, subject to each service's terms.
    • Interest on reserves: Value: Yes; Note: Eligible institutions earn interest on reserve balances.
    • Discount window: Value: Yes; Note: Depository institutions can borrow from the discount window if they meet its credit and collateral rules.
    • Intraday credit: Value: Yes; Note: Daytime overdrafts are allowed within caps under the Fed's Payment System Risk policy.
    Legal basis
    Federal Reserve Act (Reserve Banks 'may' receive deposits, 12 U.S.C. 342; Monetary Control Act pricing and access, 12 U.S.C. 248a); Board Guidelines for Evaluating Account and Services Requests (Aug 15, 2022); Reserve Bank Operating Circular 1. Buying Federal Reserve Bank stock (membership), which the OCC requires of new national trust banks, is a separate step and does not by itself give an account.
    Status
    in force
    Evidence through
    2026-10-19
    Verified on web
    Yes
    Open questions
    The Board's May 2026 proposal would also revise these guidelines; the final form is not yet published.
    Sources: Federal Reserve Board — final Guidelines for Evaluating Account and Services Requests (three-tier review) (2022-08-15) · Federal Register 2026-10375 (91 FR 30627), Docket OP-1878 — Proposed revisions to the Payment System Risk policy and Account Access Guidelines (Payment Accounts) (2026-05-26) · Tenth Circuit opinion, Custodia Bank v. Federal Reserve Board, No. 24-8024 (2025-10-31) · Second Circuit docket 25-1144, Banco San Juan Internacional v. FRBNY (2026-05-13)

    Limited-purpose ("skinny") account — Kraken Financial's one-off accountIn force

    Checked through: 2026-10-19 · Also shown on: Account types
    Who can get it
    One institution so far: Kraken Financial, approved by the Kansas City Fed on Mar 4, 2026 under existing law. The Kansas City Fed says this did not create a new account category or widen who is eligible; Fed Vice Chair Bowman called it a pilot for this one institution.
    What it allows
    • Payment services: Value: partial; Note: Fedwire Funds only, with any payment that would overdraw the account rejected automatically. Kraken says no FedNow or ACH.
    • Interest on reserves: Value: No; Note: No interest on balances.
    • Discount window: Value: No; Note: No discount-window credit.
    • Intraday credit: Value: No; Note: No intraday credit; end-of-day balance is capped (amount not published).
    Legal basis
    Kansas City Fed's discretion under the Federal Reserve Act and the Board's 2022 Account Access Guidelines; one-year initial term.
    Status
    in force
    Evidence through
    2026-10-19
    Verified on web
    Yes
    Open questions
    Term dates and whether the account has been used (see the Kraken row).
    Sources: Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City — Approves limited account (Payward Financial dba Kraken Financial) (2026-03-04) · Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City — Supplemental information regarding Kraken Financial account (2026-05-08)

    Special-purpose Payment Account (proposed)Proposed

    Checked through: 2026-10-19 · Also shown on: Account types
    Who can get it
    Any institution legally eligible for a Reserve Bank account, whatever its tier; an institution could not hold both a Payment Account and a master account. Reserve Banks would decide requests, generally within 90 days of a complete file. The proposal does not widen legal eligibility.
    What it allows
    • Payment services: Value: partial; Note: Only services where overdrafts can be rejected automatically: Fedwire Funds, FedNow, the National Settlement Service, and Fedwire Securities transfers free of payment. No FedACH and no securities delivery-versus-payment.
    • Interest on reserves: Value: No; Note: No interest on balances (Regulation D proposal).
    • Discount window: Value: No; Note: No discount-window credit (Regulation A proposal).
    • Intraday credit: Value: No; Note: No intraday credit. End-of-day balance capped at a level set per institution, at most $1 billion; no limit on balances during the day.
    Legal basis
    Proposed new Part IV of the Fed's Payment System Risk policy and revised Account Access Guidelines (Docket OP-1878, Federal Register 2026-10375, 91 FR 30627), with amendments to Regulation D (2026-10377) and Regulation A (2026-10376). Board approved May 20, 2026; published May 26, 2026; comments closed July 27, 2026. The Board asked Reserve Banks to pause Tier 3 decisions until it finishes. Preceded by a Dec 23, 2025 request for information.
    Status
    proposed
    Evidence through
    2026-10-19
    Verified on web
    Yes
    Open questions
    No final rule found through 2026-10-19
    Sources: Federal Reserve Board press release — Payment Account proposal and request that Reserve Banks pause Tier 3 decisions (2026-05-20) · Federal Register 2026-10375 (91 FR 30627), Docket OP-1878 — Proposed revisions to the Payment System Risk policy and Account Access Guidelines (Payment Accounts) (2026-05-26) · Federal Register 2026-10377 — Regulation D proposal: no interest on Payment Account balances (2026-05-26) · Federal Register 2026-10376 — Regulation A proposal: no discount-window credit for Payment Accounts (2026-05-26) · Federal Register 2025-23712 — Request for information on a Reserve Bank Payment Account prototype (2025-12-23)

    No Fed account (using a correspondent bank)In force

    Checked through: 2026-10-19 · Also shown on: Account types
    Who can get it
    Any firm with a bank relationship. The firm's payments settle through another bank's Fed account (for example, Kraken customer wires still go through Dart Bank). The Fed's database lists institutions that settle through another depository institution's account as having access this way.
    What it allows
    • Payment services: Value: partial; Note: Indirect only, on the correspondent bank's terms and hours.
    • Interest on reserves: Value: No; Note: None from the Fed directly; any interest comes from the correspondent bank.
    • Discount window: Value: No; Note: None from the Fed directly.
    • Intraday credit: Value: No; Note: None from the Fed directly; any credit is from the correspondent.
    Legal basis
    Private contract with the correspondent bank.
    Status
    in force
    Evidence through
    2026-10-19
    Verified on web
    Yes
    Sources: Federal Reserve Board — Master Account and Services Database: About (data current as of Aug 31, 2026; page updated Sep 18, 2026) (2026-09-18)

    Request for Information and Comment on Reserve Bank Payment Account PrototypeOfficial

    Date: 2025-12-23
    Date
    2025-12-23
    Agency
    Federal Reserve System
    Type
    Notice
    Summary
    The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (Board) seeks public input on a special purpose Reserve Bank account prototype (a Payment Account) tailored to the risks and needs of institutions focused on payments innovation. A Payment Account holder would be expected to use its account for the express purpose of clearing and settling the institution's payment activity. Payment Accounts would be designed to pose limited risk to the Federal Reserve Banks (Reserve Banks) and the overall payment system, and Reserve Banks would generally conduct a streamlined review of requests for these accounts. Any institution that is legally eligible for Federal Reserve accounts or services (accounts and services) under the Federal Reserve Act would be eligible to request a Payment Account from a Reserve Bank. The Payment Account protype does not seek to expand or otherwise change legal eligibility for access to accounts and services.
    Tags
    payment account, reserve bank account
    Record kind
    official
    Sources: federalregister.gov

    Prohibition on Use of Reputation Risk or Other Supervisory Tools To Encourage or Compel Banking Organizations To Engage in Politicized or Unlawful DiscriminationOfficial

    Date: 2026-02-26
    Date
    2026-02-26
    Agency
    Federal Reserve System
    Type
    Proposed Rule
    Summary
    The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (Board) is inviting public comment on a notice of proposed rulemaking (proposal or proposed rule) that would codify the removal of reputation risk from the Board's supervisory programs. The proposal would prohibit the Board from encouraging or compelling Board-supervised banking organizations to deny or condition the provision of banking or other financial products or services to an individual or business based on their constitutionally protected political or religious beliefs, associations, speech, or conduct, or based on involvement by the individual or business in politically disfavored but lawful business activities perceived to present reputation risk.
    Tags
    reputation risk
    Record kind
    official

    Prohibition on the Use of Reputation Risk by RegulatorsOfficial

    Date: 2026-04-10
    Date
    2026-04-10
    Agency
    Treasury Department — Comptroller of the Currency
    Type
    Rule
    Summary
    The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation are adopting a final rule to codify the elimination of reputation risk from their supervisory programs. Among other things, the rule prohibits the agencies from criticizing or taking adverse action against an institution on the basis of reputation risk. The rule also prohibits the agencies from requiring, instructing, or encouraging an institution to close an account, to refrain from providing an account, product, or service, or to modify or terminate any product or service on the basis of a person or entity's political, social, cultural, or religious views or beliefs, constitutionally protected speech, or solely on the basis of politically disfavored but lawful business activities perceived to present reputation risk. The rule further forbids the agencies from taking any supervisory action or other adverse action against an institution, a group of institutions, or the institution-affiliated parties of any institution that is designed to punish or discourage an individual or group from engaging in any lawful political, social, cultural, or religious activities, constitutionally protected speech, or, for political reasons, lawful business activities that the agencies or its personnel disagree with or disfavor.

    Federal securities or derivatives-market authorityCurrent

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: License route

    Supervise and authorize

    A legally classified securities-market or derivatives-market activity calls for the applicable SEC or CFTC registration, designation, supervision, or rule route.
    Basis
    Federal securities laws and the Commodity Exchange Act, each within its statutory perimeter.
    Conditions
    • Classify the instrument, contract, and activity.
    • Identify the exact entity and applicable SEC, CFTC, or SRO route.

    Eligible categories

    • Commodity Futures Trading Commission
    • SEC or CFTC offices acting under delegated authority
    • Self-regulatory organizations only within their separate statutory rulemaking roles
    Limit
    Neither tokenization nor a technical ledger decides securities/commodity classification or creates SEC/CFTC permission.

    current

    CFTC swap reporting counterparty or registered-entity routeCurrent

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: License route
    Jobs served
    Report trades and retain regulatory records
    Firms and public bodies named
    None named yet
    Trigger
    The transaction is a CFTC-regulated swap and Part 45 assigns a reporting counterparty or reporting task to a SEF, DCM, or DCO.
    Basis
    CEA swap-data framework and 17 CFR Parts 45 and 49.
    Conditions
    • Classify the instrument as a CFTC-regulated swap and identify the reporting hierarchy or registered-entity rule.
    • Select an appropriate SDR and meet its data, validation, timing, and access requirements.
    • A counterparty may contract with a facilitator to submit data, but preserve the assigned reporting party's responsibility and evidence of successful acceptance.
    Eligible categories
    • swap dealer
    • major swap participant
    • other reporting counterparty as allocated by Part 45
    • swap execution facility
    • designated contract market
    • derivatives clearing organization
    • third-party reporting facilitator acting for the responsible reporter
    Limit
    A delegate submits or facilitates only under the responsible party's arrangement; it is neither automatically the reporting counterparty nor an SDR. A generic blockchain log or oracle feed is not an SDR report.
    State
    current
    Sources: CFTC swap-data reporting rules · CFTC final Part 45 rulemaking: third-party reporting facilitation (2011-12-20)

    4 · Transition gates: where a technology qualifies, and where it does not

    Fourteen requirements in three groups

    · 26 rows

    Immutability, pause keys or upgradeability do not decide legal remedy or recover irreversible loss.
    External joins
    Decision authority, Correction procedure, Recovery liquidity, Final loss rule
    Fits
    • Fit: core · Maturity: R4 controls / R5 unproved · Note: Transfer restrictions, correction and reissue can operate within appointed product records.
    • Fit: core · Maturity: R4 incumbent / token stress open · Note: Rulebooks, official records and detokenization provide correction paths; token-path failure proof remains open.
    • Fit: core · Maturity: R4 controls / stress-specific · Note: Administrative and redemption controls can respond to events; final holder loss depends on law and reserves.
    • Fit: supporting · Maturity: R4 tooling · Note: Pause, freeze, recovery and policy tools can contain damage under an authorized operator.
    • Fit: supporting · Maturity: R4 custody controls · Note: Segregation and authorization can support recovery; insolvency and final loss remain legal questions.
    • Fit: supporting · Maturity: R4 surveillance tooling · Note: Detection can initiate investigation but does not adjudicate or allocate loss.
    • Fit: conditional · Maturity: R3 bounded path · Note: Participant and bank procedures may resolve exceptions; published end-to-end stress allocation remains open.
    • Fit: conditional · Maturity: R3-R4 route-specific · Note: Application governance can manage corrections while participant books and legal remedies remain distributed.
    • Fit: conditional · Maturity: R1-R2 · Note: Recovery and wind-down controls require operating evidence under the temporary registration.
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Economics and legacy retirement

    Home checked through: 2026-09-22
    Group
    Close and survive
    Number
    14
    Question
    Does the full route lower all-in cost or materially improve service after liquidity, compliance, cyber and parallel-run costs?
    Proof
    Recurring production, full-cost comparison, failure proof and actual decommissioning of redundant books or buffers.
    Boundary
    No reviewed stack qualifies for the complete R6 state while material parallel books, external cash and incumbent backstops remain.
    External joins
    Full-cost measurement, Recurring material volume, Failure proof, Decommissioning approval
    Fits
    • Fit: conditional · Maturity: R4 component / R6 unproved · Note: High-volume execution does not establish lower end-to-end institutional cost or legacy retirement.
    • Fit: conditional · Maturity: R4 component / R6 unproved · Note: Throughput and fees do not capture legal, custody, liquidity, accounting and parallel-run costs.
    • Fit: conditional · Maturity: R4 component / R6 unproved · Note: Recurring token use does not prove bank, reserve, payout and compliance duplication can retire.
    • Fit: conditional · Maturity: R3 token path / R6 unproved · Note: Bounded production must show recurring economics and retirement of duplicative records or processes.
    • Fit: conditional · Maturity: R3-R4 component / R6 unproved · Note: Completed transactions and live applications need route-level cost, scale and stress receipts.
    • Fit: conditional · Maturity: R3 component / R6 unproved · Note: Live pairings must prove recurring scale, full economics and retirement of external reconciliation.
    • Fit: supporting · Maturity: R4 service / R6 unproved · Note: Middleware economics can improve a route without proving the whole route is cheaper or self-sufficient.
    • Fit: conditional · Maturity: R4 component / R6 unproved · Note: Bank-token operation can be material while incumbent balance-sheet and settlement anchors remain.
    • Fit: conditional · Maturity: R3-R4 component / R6 unproved · Note: Corridor operation must prove full cost and reduced trapped liquidity across participants.
    • Fit: conditional · Maturity: R4 component / R6 unproved · Note: Recognized settlement money remains jurisdiction- and route-specific, with system-retirement proof still needed.
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    5 · Courts: who gets a Fed account, and who can remove a Fed governor

    The cases

    · 6 rows

    Read from: _Workspace/Indexes/masters/records/courts.json › cases

    Trump v. Cook — SCOTUS No. 25A312; below D.D.C. and D.C. Circuit

    Record checked through: 2026-10-19 · Also shown on: In court
    Caption
    Trump v. Cook — SCOTUS No. 25A312; below D.D.C. and D.C. Circuit
    Question
    May the President immediately remove a sitting Fed Governor "for cause," without notice and a chance to answer — and is the Governor's tenure protection constitutional?
    State
    Stay denied 2026-06-29 (Roberts for a 5-4 majority): courts may review 'cause', a removal needs notice and a chance to respond, and Cook stays in office while the case continues. On 2026-10-07 the President named a committee to decide whether cause exists; its hearing is set for 2026-11-05.
    Stakes
    One Governor's chair is one FOMC vote — and the ruling drew the constitutional fence around the Fed itself: the one agency the removal revolution doesn't reach.
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Trump v. Slaughter — SCOTUS No. 25-332; below D.D.C.

    Record checked through: 2026-10-19 · Also shown on: In court
    Caption
    Trump v. Slaughter — SCOTUS No. 25-332; below D.D.C.
    Question
    Does the FTC's for-cause removal protection survive Article II?
    State
    Reversed 6–3 on 2026-06-29: FTC protection unconstitutional; Humphrey's Executor no longer shields the modern commission. The Fed was expressly treated as a distinct historical arrangement.
    Stakes
    Every independent financial commission except the Fed is now removable at will — the President's hand reaches SEC-style bodies, and only the central bank keeps its carve-out.
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Custodia Bank v. Federal Reserve Board & FRB Kansas City — D. Wyo.; 10th Cir. 24-8024; SCOTUS No. 26-62

    Record checked through: 2026-10-19 · Also shown on: In court
    Caption
    Custodia Bank v. Federal Reserve Board & FRB Kansas City — D. Wyo.; 10th Cir. 24-8024; SCOTUS No. 26-62
    Question
    Does statutory eligibility give a state-chartered bank a right to a Reserve Bank master account?
    State
    Tenth Circuit (2025-10-31): eligibility for a master account is not an entitlement. Custodia petitioned the Supreme Court on 2026-07-10 (No. 26-62); the Fed opposed review on 2026-10-13. The Court has not yet decided whether to hear it.
    Stakes
    THE gate case. Every crypto bank, fintech trust, and state money experiment needs the Fed's rails; whether access is a right or a favor is now before the Court — or settled for a generation if cert is denied.
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Banco San Juan Internacional v. FRBNY & Board — S.D.N.Y.; 2d Cir. 25-1144

    Record checked through: 2026-10-19 · Also shown on: In court
    Caption
    Banco San Juan Internacional v. FRBNY & Board — S.D.N.Y.; 2d Cir. 25-1144
    Question
    May a Reserve Bank terminate an existing master account under contract and risk process?
    State
    Affirmed 2026-05-13: no statutory right to continued service; FRBNY's termination authority stands.
    Stakes
    The gate swings both ways — an account once granted can be taken. Second and Tenth Circuits now converge on Reserve Bank discretion.
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Fourth Corner Credit Union v. FRB Kansas City — D. Colo.; 10th Cir. 16-1016 (2017)

    Record checked through: 2026-10-19 · Also shown on: In court
    Caption
    Fourth Corner Credit Union v. FRB Kansas City — D. Colo.; 10th Cir. 16-1016 (2017)
    Question
    Must a Reserve Bank serve a state-chartered cannabis credit union?
    State
    Fractured 1-1-1 judgment; amended lawful-purpose complaint allowed; no entitlement established. Later Custodia law rejects the entitlement reading.
    Stakes
    The first crack at the gate question — three judges, three theories, no rule — showing why Custodia's published holding matters.
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    TNB USA v. FRBNY — S.D.N.Y. 1:18-cv-07978 (2020)

    Record checked through: 2026-10-19 · Also shown on: In court
    Caption
    TNB USA v. FRBNY — S.D.N.Y. 1:18-cv-07978 (2020)
    Question
    Did FRBNY unlawfully stall a "narrow bank" built to pass interest-on-reserves to depositors?
    State
    Dismissed as unripe (2020) — no final denial, no merits ruling.
    Stakes
    The narrow-bank idea — 100%-reserve money without lending — died in the waiting room, not in court. The gate can win by never answering.
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    What is uncertain

    • Primary sources only (Katie, 2026-10-19): official records and the actor's own documents. News, newsletters, blogs and law-firm summaries were removed on 2026-10-19; what rested on them is held in masters/_held/needs_primary_source_2026-10-19.json.
    • U.S. research: all 26 function families now have at least one bounded route. This is coverage of the selected functions, not every legal alternative or eligible institution. Named profiles retain their source dates; current permissions, appointments and access must be established for the arrangement.
    • Functional fit is not legal qualification. Legal qualification is not operation. Operation is not recurring scale, failure proof or legacy retirement.
    • A conditional approval is not a charter: the firm must meet the conditions before it can open.
    • Two institutions and one queue count are marked needs_primary_source in the master; they carry that label here.
    • The OCC Crypto Charters and National Trust Banks package (2026-10-13) has no JSON registry in this workbench (README only); its decisions are carried on the institution rows and the dated charter record above.
